_about: The Pitch Coach's question bank. A question with {placeholders} is tailored: it is asked only when seed/ has the numbers to fill it. tests = what the investor is really checking. strong = what a strong answer has. hint = your own numbers to have ready.

questions.q: Your SOM is {som_share} of a {sam} SAM in {som_years} years. What gets you the first 1,000 customers?
questions.tests: whether the market slide connects to a real go-to-market
questions.strong: one channel, its cost per customer, and how many customers it has already produced

questions.q: Your market size rests on an assumption ({assumption}). Where does that number come from?
questions.tests: whether you know which of your numbers are guesses
questions.strong: the source, or an honest 'it is an assumption' and how you will test it
questions.hint: Every assumption is listed by market.py show.

questions.q: Who exactly is the customer, and how many of them are there?
questions.strong: one customer, one number, one source

questions.q: Why is this a venture-scale market and not a nice small business?
questions.strong: the path from your first city to a large yearly revenue, with numbers

questions.q: What happens to demand in a recession?
questions.strong: how your customer behaved in the last downturn, with a number

questions.q: {c1_name} has {c1_ratings} ratings. Why will {customers} switch?
questions.tests: whether your edge is big enough to beat habit
questions.strong: the pain, with evidence, and the moment someone switches

questions.q: {c1_name}'s reviews are about {c1_weak}. What stops {c1_name} from fixing that next quarter?
questions.strong: why the incumbent's business model makes the fix costly for them

questions.q: {c2_name} users complain about {c2_weak}. How do you make sure that never happens to you?
questions.strong: the mechanism, what it costs, and what happens when it fails

questions.q: Who else is building this right now?
questions.strong: names, what they do differently, and why you win anyway

questions.q: What is your unfair advantage?
questions.strong: one specific thing: a channel, data, a cost, a team fact

questions.q: Why hasn't the market leader already done this?
questions.tests: whether you understand the incumbent's incentives
questions.strong: the cost or conflict that stops them, with a number

questions.q: What have you proven so far?
questions.strong: numbers: users, revenue, retention, a waitlist, a pilot, with dates

questions.q: How fast are you growing, week over week?
questions.strong: one growth rate over a stated period

questions.q: What does a customer who stays look like, and why do they stay?
questions.strong: a cohort number and the reason in the customer's words

questions.q: What did you learn that surprised you?
questions.strong: a specific finding and what you changed because of it

questions.q: What does your {take_rate} take rate leave after {provider_pay}?
questions.tests: whether the business makes money per order
questions.strong: revenue and contribution per order, in dollars
questions.hint: Per {unit}: {price} price, you keep {revenue_per_order}, {contribution_per_order} after costs.

questions.q: Your LTV:CAC is {ltv_cac}. What CAC did you assume, and what have you actually paid?
questions.strong: the assumed CAC, the real CAC so far, and the channel
questions.hint: CAC {cac}, LTV {ltv}, paid back in {cac_payback} months.

questions.q: You break even in month {breakeven_month}. What has to be true for that?
questions.strong: the two or three drivers and how sensitive breakeven is to each

questions.q: What is your gross margin, and how does it change at scale?
questions.strong: the margin today and the one cost that falls with scale

questions.q: How do you set your price, and what happens if you raise it 20%?
questions.strong: how you tested price and what customers did

questions.q: What does it cost you to get one customer today, and through which channel?
questions.strong: a dollar figure from real spend, the channel, and the payback in months

questions.q: Why are you the team to build this?
questions.strong: a specific past result that maps to this problem

questions.q: Who is your next key hire, and why?
questions.strong: the gap, the role and when it starts

questions.q: How do the founders split decisions, and what happens when you disagree?
questions.strong: a real example

questions.q: Are you full time, and how much runway do you personally have?
questions.strong: a straight yes and a date

questions.q: Why now? Why couldn't this have been built five years ago?
questions.strong: one change in the world, with a date or a number

questions.q: What changes in the next two years that makes this bigger?
questions.strong: a trend with a source

questions.q: What would make this a bad time to start?
questions.strong: the headwind, named, and why you start anyway

questions.q: The model shows a peak burn of {peak_burn} a month. What do you cut if the raise takes six months longer?
questions.strong: the cut list in order, and the runway it buys

questions.q: What is the single biggest risk to this company?
questions.strong: one risk, named plainly, and the test that retires it

questions.q: What has to go right that you do not control?
questions.strong: the dependency and your plan B

questions.q: What regulation, liability or insurance issue could hurt you?
questions.strong: the specific rule or exposure and how you handle it

questions.q: You are raising {raise}. Walk me through where it goes and what it gets you.
questions.tests: whether the money buys a milestone
questions.strong: the use of funds and the milestone it reaches before the next round

questions.q: {inv_first}'s record: {inv_deal}. How is {startup} different, and do you want {inv_firm} to lead?
questions.tests: whether you did your homework on this investor
questions.strong: what you know about their deal, the difference in one line, and a clear yes on the role you want

questions.q: Who else is in the round, and who is leading?
questions.strong: names or the honest state, and the close date

questions.q: What valuation or cap are you raising at, and why?
questions.strong: the number and the comparable rounds behind it

questions.q: What milestones will you hit before you raise again?
questions.tests: a plan for the next round
questions.strong: two or three numbers with dates
